Synopsis:
    The article questions whether traditional bear market definitions (20% decline) remain meaningful for highly volatile, AI-driven tech indexes like the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), KOSPI, and Nasdaq 100. Both SOX and KOSPI technically entered bear markets in July despite remaining massively up year-to-date. Analysts are debating alternative frameworks incorporating volatility-adjusted thresholds, moving averages, duration of decline, and macro conditions. The core risk flagged is that outdated labels may cause investors to prematurely exit positions and miss AI-driven gains, with S&P 500 semiconductor earnings estimated to grow 114.7% this year.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US stock market pricing?
Relevance: YES — directly discusses US tech index pricing dynamics, investor positioning behavior, and the distorting effect of AI-driven volatility on market classification frameworks. Indirect reference to interest rates as a structural bear market condition.

The article synthesizes existing views rather than surfacing a new, unexpected risk. The 114.7% semiconductor earnings growth estimate adds some incremental forward-looking signal.
